questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The most important aspects were location and the course catalog. I always wanted to experience the American system. Dartmouth offered a perfect combination of high academically quality, and beautiful nature close to bigger cities like Boston and New York

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Indeed, it was an experience for life. It was exciting, educational, inspiring and fun, but it was also challenging and at times tough. People should be prepared that studying abroad takes a lot of energy, but it is definitely worth it.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. Dartmouth sends out a lot of information upon arrival, and if you have any other questions you can always contact their counselor for exchange students, who is really sweet and helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Arrival was a bit overwhelming, but the administrative staff were extremely helpful. I also found support in the other exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
As an undergraduate exchange student you are staying at campus, like the majority of American students.
The housing for exchange students were quite good compared to some of the houses American students lived in. There is a chance that you will have a roommate, but you can apply for a single, which I did and got both terms. If you strongly prefer a single room you can check out the different community houses - they tend to have open spots. Though, having a roommate can have its benefits a well - it will probably be another exchange student.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: As an undergraduate you are signed up for one of the schools meal plans providing most meals. Depending on the house you end you end up in, the cooking facilities are quite limited. I personally enjoyed the meal plan.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It can of course be a challenge living so close to other people, especially because the American students tend to be younger. The walls are quite thin and the bathrooms were sometimes a bit gross. But overall I had a great experience. The common areas were cleaned every day and the rooms were nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Dartmouth is a very tiny place. I personally loved the atmosphere where everyone lives together at campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was mostly the visa thing that was demanding. The school was helpful and made the proces easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to take a language test. The rest is just online forms. Be aware of the emails they send you, especially the one providing you with a Dartmouth email . All important informations like housing will be send to this.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could always email the counselor for exchange students. The replies came within a few days, often just hours.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Some of them I didn't get in the first try, but I recommend emailling the professor. In my experience they like having exchange students in there classes, and are open to help you if they can. Also, be patient. The first week is drop/add, so you can be lucky that a spot opens up.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great courses, small classes and incredible professors.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: According to Dartmouth rules you can only take undergraduate courses tough you are a master student in Denmark. However, the level is pretty high so it doesn't really matter. They working load is extreme compared to KU. You should be prepared at spending a lot of time studying for class and finals.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A LOT of readings. Especially in the political science departement. Their quarter system makes it quite intense, since you have both midterms and finals within ten weeks. The classes are small and you will have a close relation to your professors, who also offer office hours, which is great for sparring. But they also expect a lot from you, and the amount of quizzes and assignments is a bit crazy. It is hardcore, but you will learn a lot, and their courses are great.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
First term: 
The American Political System 
War and Peace in Modern Age 
Fall and Rise of Great Powers 

Second term:
Political Misinformation and Conspiracy Theories
Introduction to the Middle East 
Inequality and American Democracy (seminar)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
War and Peace in Modern Age 
Political Misinformation and Conspiracy Theories
Inequality and American Democracy (seminar)

I recommend taking a seminar. It is more demanding but worth it. 
Also I recommend courses with Brendan Nyhan who is in expert in his field, Benjamin Valentino and Herchel Nachlis. They are all great professors.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Everything from visa to language tests are quite expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I was surprised how expensive it is to live in the US. Going out for coffee og dinner is just as expensive as in Copenhagen

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The social environment is very different than the Danish. 
They are mainly socialising through clubs or their soroties/frats, which can be a bit complicated as an exchange students. You really have to make an effort, but it is possible. And the school offers a lot of other things to do like a cinema, creative workshops, and outdoor activities

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All sorts of things. They are very sporty, but I am not sure how easy it is to join a sports team due to our limited time. But there is a free gym, free hikes offered in the weekend etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I strongly recommend going on the trips arranged by the Outdoor club. Its free and a great way to see the area and meet new people. I also enjoyed their cinema (The Hop) and the jewelry workshop (Also at the Hop)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I really liked Boston. But you can also take a bus to NY directly from campus. There is also a lot of nice things to see in New England, though it requires a car.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: A bit challenging. They are much more introvert than I expected. And their extreme focus on school makes it a bit difficult to get to know them, but be patient. Usually there is around 8-10 exchange students and a lot of international students, who can provide you with support as well.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I personally had succes in sending emails out to people from my classes who I though were nice. Join the outdoor trips.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They are younger, and less open than you might expect. They work hard, and it sometimes takes their focus from social events. But they are also extremely kind if you are patient and give them a change.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The opportunity to focus on school without any other obligations. 
The beautiful nature, the American politeness, and the academically connection the the professors.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The workload is quite extreme, so don't expect it to be a holiday 
The location is a bit isolated, at times boring, but it is also beautiful. Try to benefit from the many opportunities for skiing, iceskating, hikes etc. 
Use your professors knowledge, they will love to help you in any way

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Again I want you to be aware of the workload. I found it a bit overwhelming. But it is manageable once you find a rhythm.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The nature and the academically part

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The social scene and the workload

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Dartmouth is a great place, where you will learn a whole lot both academically, about the US and not at least yourself

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
